top.title: New York says no more subscriptions for in-car features—or does it?
top.description: Car buyers in New York may find the cost of ownership reduces a little next year. Maybe. Governor Kathy Hochul signed a bill yesterday that bans car companies and dealerships from locking up car features behind a subscription, a law that goes into effect on February 27 next year. “People spending their hard-earned money on a car shouldn’t have to fork over even more money for features that should automatically come with the car. My message to car companies is clear: this kind of deceptive business model isn’t going to fly in New York State. Keep your hands out of New Yorkers’ wallets,” the governor said. In the old days, the only options you paid to use after you bought a car were mods or upgrades you installed after the fact. That started to change with services like General Motors’ OnStar, which introduced telematics to the vehicle—for a monthly fee. Read full article Comments

top.title: Coldcard Postmortem Says Weak Seeds, Not Hacked Devices, Drove Bitcoin Thefts
top.description: Bitcoin Magazine Coldcard Postmortem Says Weak Seeds, Not Hacked Devices, Drove Bitcoin Thefts Coinkite on Tuesday published its full postmortem on the Coldcard seed-generation flaw that let thieves drain bitcoin from customer wallets starting in July, saying no device was hacked and that the stolen keys were rebuilt offline from weak seeds. The 18-page report , dated Nov. 23 and modeled on a National Transportation Safety Board accident report, lays out how the defect shipped in Coldcard firmware from March 29, 2021, through July 30, 2026, and why years of outside reviews missed it. “The losses are real and, for some customers, life-changing. No report or firmware update can undo that. We are sorry,” Coinkite wrote. A silent swap in the random number generator A seed is the list of recovery words that controls a bitcoin wallet, and it is only as safe as the randomness used to create it. Coldcard devices were supposed to draw that randomness from the hardware random number generator built into their STM32 chip. Instead, a firmware setting switched that hardware source off, and a safeguard in Coinkite’s libNgU code library failed to catch it. Seed generation quietly fell back to Yasmarang, a predictable software generator built into MicroPython, the programming environment the firmware runs on. Nothing crashed, and the devices produced normal-looking seed words. Coinkite estimates affected seeds carried roughly 40 bits of effective security on the older Mk2 and Mk3 models and about 72 bits on the Mk4, Mk5 and Q, against an intended 128 bits. That shrinks the pool of possible seeds enough for attackers to search it offline. The report says Coinkite’s release checks confirmed the hardware code was present, but never confirmed that seed generation actually reached it. At least 15 independent review efforts since 2021 also missed the flaw, including two paid third-party reviews and an AI-assisted firmware review this year that produced 85 candidate findings. Hundreds of Coldcard owners report losses Unexpected transactions from affected seeds began July 29. Coinkite said it identified the defect the next day, after users discovered thefts, and shipped fixed firmware for every supported release track on July 31. As of Nov. 18, Coinkite had received about 300 loss-related support tickets tied to 242 customer accounts, or about 0.21% of its estimated Coldcard user base. The company’s blog post cites 236 accounts. Because Coldcard is self-custodial, Coinkite can only count losses that customers report, and it says the true number is likely higher. The report cites Galaxy Research figures showing 1,778.84 BTC stolen from more than 8,600 addresses, worth about $107 million at today’s price. Galaxy pegged losses above $115 million in August, based on prices when the coins were taken, and white hats later moved some exposed coins into a recovery trust. top.title: Katsina suspends Emir of Daura’s engagements over assault allegation, launches investigation
top.description: By Fauziyya Lawal, Katsina The Katsina State Government has constituted an investigative committee to probe allegations of sexual assault involving the Emir of Daura, Alhaji Umar Faruk Umar, and a foreign tourist. The government also announced the suspension of the traditional ruler’s official engagements and travels pending the outcome of the investigation. The decisions were contained in a statement issued on Tuesday by the Commissioner for Information and Culture, Dr Bala Salisu Zango, on behalf of the state government. According to the statement, Governor Dikko Umaru Radda expressed serious concern over the allegations, describing the matter as one requiring careful attention and appropriate action. The governor consequently directed the immediate constitution of an investigative committee to examine the allegations and advise the government on the appropriate course of action. The statement said the decision was informed by the seriousness of the allegations and the need to establish the facts surrounding the reported incident. The government assured the public that justice would be served, adding that the findings and recommendations of the committee would be fully implemented. It said the suspension of the Emir’s official engagements and travels was among the measures taken by the government while the investigation lasted. The government also appealed to residents and members of the public to remain calm, law-abiding and refrain from actions capable of disrupting public peace. It urged residents to continue with their normal activities, reaffirming its commitment to handling the matter appropriately. The outcome of the committee’s investigation is expected to guide further action by the state government. top.title: Man Utd win appeal over Yoro red card
top.description: Leny Yoro’s one-match suspension for the red card he was shown in Manchester United’s 4-0 mauling by Liverpool has been overturned, the Football Association announced on Tuesday. The French defender was dismissed in the eighth minute at Anfield for bringing down Alexander Isak as he advanced towards goal, with referee Sam Barrott deciding Yoro had denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity. United indicated on Monday that they intended to appeal for wrongful dismissal and a one-match suspension for the centre-back has now been lifted. The FA said the written reasons for their decision would be published in due course. Yoro, 21, will now be available for Saturday’s 1500 GMT kick-off against Brentford at Old Trafford. Dominik Szoboszlai scored Liverpool’s opening goal directly from the free-kick awarded for Yoro’s challenge and the home team cantered to an easy win. One question raised over the Yoro incident was whether Isak had the ball sufficiently under control for it to count as denial of an obvious goalscoring opportunity. United captain Bruno Fernandes told the BBC after the match that it was “never a red card”, adding: “I think it’s too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR, seated, with such a long time to see and put it back, go forward, put it back, do it in slow motion, whatsoever. “To make a mistake like this can change a game. But obviously, then, it’s not because of them that we concede the goal from the free-kick, but it changes completely the flow of the game.” Mauricio Pochettino’s Manchester United tenure got off to the worst possible start at Anfield, with a defeat that keeps them in the Premier League relegation zone after just one top-flight win all season. top.description: Seeks Okpebholo’s intervention over Arden Table Water By Chioma Obinna The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has faulted the Edo State Consumer Protection Committee (ESCPC) over the alleged seizure of pharmaceutical products, closure of business premises and imposition of fines on operators without proper regulatory authorisation. The agency also appealed to Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo, to intervene in the reported shutdown of Chepfets Mega Investment Nigeria Limited, manufacturer of Arden Table Water, insisting that the product’s registration was undergoing renewal and that this did not establish that it was unsafe or substandard. The Director-General of NAFDAC, Prof. Mojisola Adeyeye, raised the concerns while clarifying the agency’s position on the committee’s activities in the state. She expressed concern over reports that the committee had been using NAFDAC’s product authentication platforms to verify regulated products and make public declarations about their authenticity and quality. Adeyeye explained that access to the agency’s authentication platforms did not automatically confer regulatory authority on users or provide the technical basis for declaring products counterfeit, adulterated, injurious, safe or unsafe. NAFDAC said it recognised the importance of consumer protection and welcomed collaboration with state governments and other stakeholders in the fight against counterfeit, falsified, adulterated and substandard products. However, it stressed that such interventions must respect established regulatory boundaries and applicable laws. The agency said it was particularly concerned by reports that the committee had seized regulated products, publicly labelled some products fake or adulterated, sealed business premises and imposed fines on operators under the guise of working for NAFDAC without its authorisation or guidance. It also raised concerns over the reported deployment of NAFDAC’s Automated Product Administration and Monitoring System (NAPAMS), QR code scanner, Short Messaging Service (SMS) verification platform and other regulatory tools by the committee to assess products and make public pronouncements on their identity, authenticity, efficacy and effectiveness. According to the agency, failed QR code scans, missing registration details or inconsistencies in product packaging do not, on their own, constitute sufficient evidence that a product is counterfeit or substandard. It advised consumers and other stakeholders to report such irregularities to NAFDAC for investigation and possible laboratory analysis, urging the public to await the agency’s findings before making claims about products. top.title: Man Utd's Yoro has Anfield red card overturned
top.description: Leny Yoro was sent off for this tackle on Alexander Isak [Getty Images] Manchester United defender Leny Yoro has had the red card he was shown during Sunday's Premier League match at Liverpool overturned. The Football Association has confirmed Yoro will now be clear to face Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday. "Leny Yoro's one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal," said the FA in a statement. New United head coach Mauricio Pochettino was furious at the decision, which came just eight minutes in and, he felt, changed the course of the game, which Liverpool won 4-0. Liverpool striker Alexander Isak ran on to a ball that bounced over Matthijs de Ligt but took a heavy touch that meant the ball was likely to run through to United goalkeeper Senne Lammens even if Yoro had not brought the Swede down. Nevertheless, referee Sam Barrott sent Yoro off, drawing criticism from Pochettino. "The ball wasn't in his control," he said. "Isak, when he saw the control wasn't good, it's normal to delay, and stop to the run. In that moment that Yoro came from the back, and you go down. "But all that we play football; you know that wasn't intentional. That is never a foul." 'No-one's coming to save us' - but how can Man Utd save themselves? Sporting boss Fonseca dismisses Man Utd fragile talk United have travelled to Lisbon for their next Champions League match on Wednesday (20:00 GMT). The early dismissal of Yoro at Anfield meant Sporting had no chance to assess any changes Pochettino might have made after he replaced Michael Carrick during the international break. But despite United sitting 19th in the Premier League, Sporting boss refuses to accept United are "fragile". "I don't following the reasoning," said Fonseca, who was only appointed on 4 November after the Portuguese club bought him out of his contract at Lyon. "Manchester is a great team," he said. "I don't believe a lot that great teams are fragile. The last game they played in the Champions League, they were trailing 2-0, then won 3-2 against a very difficult opponent in Roma. "Moreover, when they have a new head coach, with such world-class players, it's extremely unpredictable to see if they will have a good day or bad day." United have not won in the Premier League since August and have conceded 19 goals in their past six games in all competitions. Yet, such was the nature of the Liverpool game, Fonseca has had to watch analysis of Pochettino's time in charge of the United States to get an idea of what to expect. "Eight minutes, red card. It's impossible to make an analysis," he said. "I tried to see Pochettino with the United States and what kind of solutions he used. There is some information but it is very difficult to predict." top.description: Credit: 'Monday Night Countdown' Troy Aikman’s tribute to Tom Jackson on Monday night was warm, heartfelt, and about one word choice away from going off without a hitch. Aikman appeared on Monday Night Countdown ahead of Bengals-Commanders to eulogize Jackson, who died Friday at 75 , and dedicated most of his remembrance to the sacrosanct Sunday night ritual that bookended nearly every week of his Hall of Fame career in Dallas. The 60-year-old Aikman recalled that arriving home after a game and tuning in to NFL Primetime was the only way a player of his generation could take stock of everything that had unfolded across the league. And for a quarterback, the show was also the definitive barometer of how his afternoon compared with the rival passers he was constantly measuring himself against. “Him and Boomer, they were so good, you know, obviously great friends, great chemistry, but what I respected probably as much as anything about that show was they could be critical and opinionated, but they didn’t attack people,” Aikman said. “Like I could throw three interceptions in a game and we could lose and I could watch Primetime and not want to go hang myself at the end of the night. They just had a respectful way of presenting the information and letting everybody know what happened, but doing it the right way, I thought. And anyone who knew Tom knew that’s who he was.” Troy Aikman: “I could throw three interceptions in a game, and we could lose, and I could watch [NFL Primetime] and not want to go hang myself at the end of the night. top.title: Titans Hold No. 1 Draft Spot As Three Teams Sit At 1-9
top.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports The Tennessee Titans still control the No. 1 spot in the 2027 NFL Draft despite a 51-30 loss to the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday. The franchise fell to 1-9 on the season, but they kept the top pick because of their weaker schedule compared to the other bad teams. The Los Angeles Chargers and Miami Dolphins also dropped to 1-9 records after their own losses, creating a three-way tie at the bottom of the league standings. According to a report , the Titans overtook the Chargers for the top spot last week after Los Angeles finally won a game, but the Chargers lost again on Sunday to the New York Jets. Now the race for the first overall selection is down to just these three clubs, and the tiebreaker rules will decide who gets the prize. Tiebreakers Favor Tennessee and Los Angeles Miami sits at third place in this race because the Dolphins face the toughest schedule of the three teams. According to reports, the Dolphins’ opponents have a .595 winning percentage, which is higher than the Titans’ .483 and the Chargers’ .531. This math means Miami needs to lose more games than the other two teams just to climb above them in the draft order. The Dolphins lost 26-9 to the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, marking their fourth straight defeat in a row. The team has been outscored 93-59 during this losing skid, and the offense has averaged under 15 points a game. Kyle Crabbs, who covers the Dolphins for Yahoo Sports, noted that the front office is not panicking despite the 1-8 start because everyone knew the roster was in a tough spot. The Quarterback Question Looms Large With the offense struggling, the need for a new quarterback has become the main topic for the Miami front office. Crabbs admitted he does not love any of the current quarterback prospects in the 2027 class. “I have a hard time falling in love with any of these guys,” Crabbs said. He listed Oklahoma State’s Drew Mestemaker, Notre Dame’s CJ Carr, and Miami’s Darien Mensah as names in play, but he feels the raw production does not reflect how Malik Willis has actually played. Willis is under contract for two more seasons, which gives the team a bridge to develop a rookie without rushing him onto the field. A Week 16 Showdown Could Decide It All A matchup at Hard Rock Stadium in Week 16 between the Chargers and Dolphins could decide which squad ends up with the poorest record. Both clubs face huge draft ramifications from that matchup as they try to secure the top pick. Miami hosts the Jets this week on Sunday, Nov. 29, before a long road trip that includes stops in Denver and Green Bay. The Dolphins have seven games left in the regular season, and two matchups against the Jets and Chargers look very winnable for the home team. top.title: NASA may get $2 billion boost as White House seeks to accelerate Artemis
top.description: As part of ongoing wrangling over the US budget for the current fiscal year, the White House on Monday night sent a list of budget exceptions to Congress it seeks in the near-term for the federal government ( see .pdf ). The list of so-called "funding anomalies" is dominated largely by appropriations for the Department of Defense, including the Golden Dome missile defense program championed by the Trump administration. However, among the highest non-defense exceptions is $2 billion for NASA's Artemis program for a "higher rate of operations." The funding represents a significant 25 percent boost for NASA's Artemis program, which received approximately $7.8 billion in fiscal year 2026. Technically, the White House is seeking to increase the annualized funding rate for Artemis to $9.8 billion, rather than immediately providing NASA with an additional $2 billion. It comes at a time when it is increasingly clear that China's lunar ambitions are as expansive as those of NASA, and there is a very good chance the Asian country reaches the Moon with astronauts before NASA can get back there. top.title: Senegal reinstated as Afcon 2025 winners by court ruling
top.description: Sadio Mane's Senegal have been confirmed as Afcon 2025 winners following their appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, giving the Teranga Lions a second continental title [Getty Images] Senegal have been reinstated as winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations after a ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport. The court's award overturns a previous decision which had stripped the West Africans of the title they won on the pitch during a chaotic final against host nation Morocco in January. The result of that match in Rabat, which saw the Teranga Lions triumph 1-0 after extra time, was overturned almost two months later when a Confederation of African Football (Caf) appeals board decreed Senegal had breached competition regulations by leaving the field of play in second-half stoppage time in protest at a penalty awarded against them. Senegal's football federation (FSF) subsequently appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas), sport's highest legal authority, with a three-man panel hearing its case behind closed doors in Lausanne on 8 October. In a unanimous verdict, the Cas panel has effectively backed the decision by referee Jean-Jacques Ndala to restart the game after Senegal returned to the field and the match was played to a conclusion. The result of the final stands and Senegal are now confirmed as Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) 2025 winners. A statement issued by Cas said the court considered that "the referee's decision to resume the match or to stop it fell definitively within his sole authority". "By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met - both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume." The FSF immediately reacted with a social media post featuring a picture of the side lifting the trophy in January captioned with the phrase "again and always champions of Africa". "The FSF welcomes this ruling with deep satisfaction," it later said in a statement. "This decision affirms, above all, the triumph of sporting fairness and reaffirms a fundamental principle: the true outcome of a match is determined exclusively on the field of play, under the protection of sports law." Meanwhile, Morocco's football federation (FRMF) expressed "surprise" at the ruling and added that it would "pursue all available legal avenues to challenge the decision". Caf is yet to comment but its president Patrice Motsepe has repeatedly said that his organisation will respect and adhere to the Cas ruling. The full grounds for the decision will be published by Cas in due course unless the parties request confidentiality. top.title: Hackensack-Teaneck Thanksgiving football game rescheduled due to storm
top.description: Another piece of North Jersey’s fading Thanksgiving football tradition is being pushed off the holiday this year, this time by the weather. The annual rivalry game between Hackensack and Teaneck, a Thanksgiving fixture dating to 1931, has been moved to Wednesday evening as a coastal storm threatens the region with heavy rain and strong winds. Kickoff is now scheduled for 6 p.m. at Teaneck High School. The change leaves one of North Jersey’s longest-running holiday rivalries without its traditional Thanksgiving morning setting. The other remaining Thanksgiving Day game, between Tenafly and Dumont, was also moved to Wednesday night because of the forecast. Story continues below photo gallery. The game was originally scheduled for Thanksgiving morning at 10:30 a.m. Kick-off will now be 6 p.m. Wednesday, Nov. 25, at Teaneck High School. “This decision was made with the safety and well-being of our student-athletes, twirlers, marching band, cheerleading teams, families, and community members as our top priority,” the Teaneck School District wrote in a statement. “We appreciate the understanding and flexibility of our students, families, alumni, and community members as we make this adjustment.” Ed Klimek, Teaneck's athletic director, said the main reason behind the decision was to allow the band, flag twirlers and cheerleaders, who had been practicing for weeks, to be able to perform. "Two years ago we played in an absolute monsoon," he said. "We can play football in the rain, but they can't perform in the rain. When I proposed this to Hackensack and to the football teams, everyone was on board." The parade to the field before the game, with the two teams’ school bands, cheerleaders and flag twirlers marching, is canceled, Klimek said. The traditional Thanksgiving Day team between the neighboring communities is one of the last played in North Jersey on the holiday. Many high school football teams have done away with the tradition of playing on Thanksgiving over the years, because of difficulties with the schedule and concerns that it would interfere with teams’ preparations for playing in championship games. The other remaining game scheduled for Thanksgiving Day between Tenafly and Dumont was also rescheduled to 6 p.m. Wednesday and will be played at Geissinger Field in Tenafly. The annual Thanksgiving Day rivalry game between Hackensack Comets and Teaneck Highwaymen dates back to 1931. Teaneck’s record for the season is 7-3. Hackensack is 4-4. Hackensack has dominated the matchup in recent years and has won the past 12 meetings between the two. top.title: Chris Johnson responds to uncalled Josh Allen unsportsmanlike penalty
top.description: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen certainly could have been called for unsportsmanlike conduct in a recent defeat of the Miami Dolphins , but wasn't. Dolphins rookie cornerback Chris Johnson and Allen were pushing and shoving at the end of an interception return by Jacob Rodriguez . Johnson was blocking Allen near a sideline when Allen appeared to fling him to ground by a facemask. Allen then shoved Johnson again when they are out of bounds. Was it a simple football play? Or should it have been a 15-yard penalty? Johnson said: "I saw J-Rod get the pick and from there on, I'm looking for a block. It just happened to be Josh Allen. I guess he didn't appreciate it much. And then we got tied up a bit." Johnson said he was surprised no flag was thrown. "Once you get into another players' helmet it's usually a flag," Johnson said. There was no broadcast replay, so here is #Bills Josh Allen’s scrap/fighting against #Dolphins corner Chris Johnson after his first interception via the All-22. #BillsMafia @BuffTrenchTalk pic.twitter.com/5txJ85EpiA — Carson Hayek (@CarsonHayek) November 23, 2026 Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley thought it was a penalty. "I saw it and our guys saw it because they were upset and then they started to talk and I said, I'll handle it," Hafley said. "And then I asked the refs. I'm not going to get into sending it to the league and everything that happened. I just, I don't understand how that is not a penalty. "And that is where I do have a hard time with that. Whatever you want to call happened, to me, that warranted a penalty. And it should have been 15 yards and the ball should have been moved up. So it happened, it's over, it was missed and we'll move on." Allen passed for 304 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions in a 26-9 victory. Allen did not have a single rushing attempt. This was likely intentional as the Bills have a game against the Chiefs on Thanksgiving. Allen, apparently, was focused on preserving his energy and health for the Kansas City game. nigeria.title: Man Utd win appeal over Yoro red card
nigeria.description: Leny Yoro’s one-match suspension for the red card he was shown in Manchester United’s 4-0 mauling by Liverpool has been overturned, the Football Association announced on Tuesday. The French defender was dismissed in the eighth minute at Anfield for bringing down Alexander Isak as he advanced towards goal, with referee Sam Barrott deciding Yoro had denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity. United indicated on Monday that they intended to appeal for wrongful dismissal and a one-match suspension for the centre-back has now been lifted. The FA said the written reasons for their decision would be published in due course. Yoro, 21, will now be available for Saturday’s 1500 GMT kick-off against Brentford at Old Trafford. Dominik Szoboszlai scored Liverpool’s opening goal directly from the free-kick awarded for Yoro’s challenge and the home team cantered to an easy win. One question raised over the Yoro incident was whether Isak had the ball sufficiently under control for it to count as denial of an obvious goalscoring opportunity. United captain Bruno Fernandes told the BBC after the match that it was “never a red card”, adding: “I think it’s too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR, seated, with such a long time to see and put it back, go forward, put it back, do it in slow motion, whatsoever. “To make a mistake like this can change a game. But obviously, then, it’s not because of them that we concede the goal from the free-kick, but it changes completely the flow of the game.” Mauricio Pochettino’s Manchester United tenure got off to the worst possible start at Anfield, with a defeat that keeps them in the Premier League relegation zone after just one top-flight win all season. nigeria.title: Ajaokuta must work again, Kogi won’t be neglected – Atiku
nigeria.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has pledged to revive the Ajaokuta Steel Mill, develop Idah River Port and complete the Kabba-Egbe road, promising to address longstanding infrastructure challenges across Kogi State. Speaking at his campaign rally in Lokoja, Atiku outlined development projects for the state’s three senatorial districts, including improved roads and water supply in Kogi East. He said the plans were aimed at creating jobs, expanding economic opportunities and making life more affordable for residents. According to the Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku said his proposed interventions would focus on turning the state’s economic potential into tangible benefits for its people. Addressing residents of Kogi East, he pledged to improve rural infrastructure and develop Idah River Port to ease the movement of agricultural produce and expand business opportunities. “To my brothers and sisters in Kogi East, I know what it means when a farmer cannot get produce to market because the road has failed, or when a family must struggle every day for clean water. We will improve your roads and water supply, and develop Idah River Port so that the region’s farmers and businesses can reach more customers,” he said. For Kogi Central, Atiku promised to revive the Ajaokuta Steel Mill, with a focus on restoring industrial production and creating employment. “Ajaokuta must finally become a working steel mill. I want its furnaces working, its gates open to skilled workers and its promise felt in the homes of the people who have waited so long. We will also support the roads and services that allow surrounding communities to benefit from that industry,” he said. In Kogi West, he pledged to complete the Kabba-Egbe road, which he said should no longer remain an unfulfilled promise. “The Kabba to Egbe road cannot remain an endless promise. We will complete it and make travel and trade easier for the communities along its route,” he stated. At the national level, Atiku also pledged to pursue the dredging of Baro Port and restore a targeted subsidy on fuel refined in Nigeria, saying the measures would help reduce transportation and production costs. The proposals formed part of his broader promise to translate infrastructure development and the state’s economic resources into employment and improved living conditions. nigeria.title: CAS explains decision to restore Senegal’s AFCON title
nigeria.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has explained why it overturned the Confederation of African Football’s (CAF) decision to award Morocco the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title, ruling that Senegal’s 1-0 victory in the final must stand. In a media release on Tuesday, the court said both teams had returned to the pitch and expressed their willingness to continue before the referee, Jean-Jacques Ndala, blew his whistle to resume play in the 109th minute. It explained that the referee’s decision to restart or stop the match fell within his authority, adding that the effects of his decision were limited to the pitch and therefore covered by the ‘field of play’ doctrine. “After having examined the arguments raised by the Parties, the Arbitral Panel considered that the Referee’s decision to resume the match or to stop it fell definitively within his sole authority. By blowing his whistle to restart play, the Referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met – both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume,” the statement said. CAS also ruled that Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations, relied upon by Morocco in its challenge, did not apply to the circumstances of the final. According to the court, the provisions are intended to determine the outcome of a match when a team’s conduct leads the referee to abandon the game permanently. The court further rejected the description of the referee’s decision as ‘arbitrary’, acknowledging the extreme tension surrounding the match but stating that his judgment did not appear to have been influenced by external factors. Consequently, CAS upheld the appeal filed by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF), set aside the CAF Appeal Board’s decision and reinstated the decision of CAF’s Disciplinary Board. The ruling confirms Senegal’s 1-0 victory over Morocco in the January 18 final, restoring the West African nation as AFCON 2025 champions. CAF had previously declared Senegal to have forfeited the final after the team temporarily left the pitch in protest during the match, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory. The decision was unanimous among the three-member CAS panel. The post CAS explains decision to restore Senegal’s AFCON title appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: Full List: 10 countries with most AFCON titles
nigeria.description: Egypt remain the most successful country in the history of the Africa Cup of Nations, AFCON with seven titles, followed by Cameroon and Ghana, who have won the continental competition five and four times respectively. Nigeria are among five countries in the top four positions, having lifted the trophy three times since making their debut at the tournament. The Super Eagles won their first AFCON title in 1980, when Nigeria hosted the competition and defeated Algeria 3-0 in the final. They secured their second crown in Tunisia in 1994, beating Zambia 2-1, before claiming their third title in South Africa in 2013 with a 1-0 victory over Burkina Faso. Côte d’Ivoire are also three-time champions, having won the tournament in 1992, 2015 and 2023. Egypt lead the all-time standings with seven titles, having dominated the competition in its early years and later enjoyed a remarkable run of three consecutive championships in 2006, 2008 and 2010. Cameroon occupy second place with five titles, while Ghana are third with four. Ghana’s last triumph came in 1982, while Cameroon’s most recent success was in 2017. Algeria and the Democratic Republic of the Congo have each won the competition twice. Algeria claimed their titles in 1990 and 2019, while DR Congo won in 1968 and 1974, when the country competed under the names Congo-Kinshasa and Zaire. Morocco are also credited with two titles, following the Confederation of African Football’s March 2026 decision to award them the 2025 AFCON trophy. Senegal had initially won the final 1-0 after extra time, but CAF’s Appeal Board later ruled that the Senegalese team had forfeited the match and recorded a 3-0 victory for Morocco. Senegal subsequently appealed the decision to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, which was expected to issue its ruling on November 24, 2026. nigeria.title: Senegal Regain AFCON Title After Appeal
nigeria.description: Senegal on Tuesday regained their Africa Cup of Nations title after winning an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the decision by the Confederation of African Football to declare Morocco the winners following a chaotic final in January. “The Court of Arbitration for Sport has upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) concerning the final of the Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025,” CAS said in a statement. The Swiss-based sports court said Senegal’s appeal had been upheld by “a unanimous decision”, and their original 1-0 victory after extra time is reinstated. In March, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) sensationally overturned the result of the final, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory, and the title, after many Senegalese players walked off the pitch in protest at a penalty given to the hosts with the game still goalless. Senegal and Morocco players line up prior the Africa Cup of Nations (CAN) final football match between Senegal and Morocco at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat on January 18, 2026. Photo by PAUL ELLIS / AFP The CAF Appeals Committee had justified its decision to overturn the result and declare Morocco champions based on Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations. Those state that if a team “refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee, it shall be considered (loser) and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition”. However, the Senegal players eventually returned to the pitch and the final carried on. The CAS panel therefore considered that the referee’s decision to restart the final showed that “the conditions for resuming the match had been met”, and that articles 82 and 84 were therefore “not applicable in this case”. The group said the attack in Uduere, Ughelli North, where gunmen opened fire while former Deputy Senate President and NDC Delta Central senatorial candidate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, was addressing supporters, exposed the dangers of inflammatory political rhetoric ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Comrade Ini Ememobong, on Tuesday, the INWC demanded that Tinubu publicly renounce his previous remarks, which it accused of encouraging hostility towards opposition parties. The statement cited Tinubu’s 2022 declaration that political power must be “grabbed, snatched and run away with”, as well as his 2026 remark that “all is fair in politics”, as examples of what it described as dangerous political messaging. “These two statements alone, coming from their leader, were the adrenaline that APC followers needed to unleash unmitigated mayhem on opposition parties,” it alleged. It also cited alleged threats by some APC figures, including Senator Fadahunsi of Osun State, the Chairman of Kuje Area Council and the party’s Edo State chairman, against citizens unwilling to vote for the ruling party. On Delta State, the group alleged that intimidation of opposition figures had become recurrent, claiming that at least two deadly attacks against opposition groups had occurred in November alone. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Coldcard Postmortem Says Weak Seeds, Not Hacked Devices, Drove Bitcoin Thefts Coinkite on Tuesday published its full postmortem on the Coldcard seed-generation flaw that let thieves drain bitcoin from customer wallets starting in July, saying no device was hacked and that the stolen keys were rebuilt offline from weak seeds. The 18-page report , dated Nov. 23 and modeled on a National Transportation Safety Board accident report, lays out how the defect shipped in Coldcard firmware from March 29, 2021, through July 30, 2026, and why years of outside reviews missed it. “The losses are real and, for some customers, life-changing. No report or firmware update can undo that. We are sorry,” Coinkite wrote. A silent swap in the random number generator A seed is the list of recovery words that controls a bitcoin wallet, and it is only as safe as the randomness used to create it. Coldcard devices were supposed to draw that randomness from the hardware random number generator built into their STM32 chip. Instead, a firmware setting switched that hardware source off, and a safeguard in Coinkite’s libNgU code library failed to catch it. Seed generation quietly fell back to Yasmarang, a predictable software generator built into MicroPython, the programming environment the firmware runs on. Nothing crashed, and the devices produced normal-looking seed words. Coinkite estimates affected seeds carried roughly 40 bits of effective security on the older Mk2 and Mk3 models and about 72 bits on the Mk4, Mk5 and Q, against an intended 128 bits. That shrinks the pool of possible seeds enough for attackers to search it offline. The report says Coinkite’s release checks confirmed the hardware code was present, but never confirmed that seed generation actually reached it. At least 15 independent review efforts since 2021 also missed the flaw, including two paid third-party reviews and an AI-assisted firmware review this year that produced 85 candidate findings. Hundreds of Coldcard owners report losses Unexpected transactions from affected seeds began July 29. Coinkite said it identified the defect the next day, after users discovered thefts, and shipped fixed firmware for every supported release track on July 31. As of Nov. 18, Coinkite had received about 300 loss-related support tickets tied to 242 customer accounts, or about 0.21% of its estimated Coldcard user base. The issuing bank promises to repay the original investment at maturity and pays a return tied to an underlying asset, in this case bitcoin through the BlackRock product. Buyers hold a claim on the bank, not bitcoin itself. If bitcoin is down at maturity, holders get 100% of their capital back. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine South Korea Unveils Crypto Bill Capping Exchange Ownership at 20% South Korea’s Financial Services Commission on Tuesday unveiled a government bill that would cap a major shareholder’s stake in a crypto exchange at 20%, open the door to domestic coin offerings and let bank-led groups issue won stablecoins. The draft, titled the Act on the Innovation of the Digital Asset Industry and Protection of Users, was presented at a Virtual Asset Committee meeting chaired by FSC Chairman Lee Eog-weon. It would replace Korea’s two-track system, built on an anti-money-laundering law and a 2024 user protection act, with a single framework covering the industry, markets and users. Lee said the law would raise trust and transparency in Korea’s digital asset market and help draw new money into the industry. He said the government would do everything it can to see the bill fully debated in the National Assembly and enacted quickly. A 20% ownership cap for exchanges Under the bill, exchanges would become “digital asset platform operators,” a designation reserved for firms that hold separate licenses for dealing, brokerage and custody. The FSC modeled the ownership limit on the rules for alternative trading systems in the stock market. Major shareholders could own up to 20%, or up to 34% with FSC approval under a presidential decree. Shares above the limit would lose their voting rights. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine DOJ Moves to Forfeit $1.1 Billion in USDC Stolen in Binance Hack The Justice Department filed a civil forfeiture complaint Monday to take ownership of more than $1.1 billion in USDC that North Korean hackers stole from Binance last month, tokens that Circle froze but says it cannot move. The complaint , filed in U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, targets all USDC held at 36 addresses across 18 blockchains. The department said the U.S. has now helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion in crypto from multiple sources since the Oct. 29 theft. On Nov. 12, the department said it had court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion, out of a joint government and industry freeze of more than $2.7 billion. A temporary restraining order issued that day was served on Circle the same day. Monday’s filing is the step that would let the government take title to the funds. Circle will mint replacement tokens Circle blocked access to the USDC on or about Oct. 29, the complaint says. But the stablecoin issuer told prosecutors it does not have the technical ability to transfer the tokens out of the blocklisted addresses, which remain under the hackers’ control. Instead, Circle has agreed to issue new USDC equal to the frozen amount and send it to the U.S. once a court enters a forfeiture order. The complaint calls those tokens “Substitute USDC.” Several of the addresses are smart contract and hot wallet addresses on Binance’s own platform. The hackers took them over in the attack and drained some, but not all, of the funds before Circle stepped in, prosecutors wrote. “It appears Binance no longer controlled them,” the complaint says. How the Binance hack worked The filing also lays out how investigators say the breach began. A Binance employee contacted by a purported recruiter agreed to a job interview and was told to download software that contained malware, which matches what the exchange said earlier this month. The infected device let the attackers plant an EIP-7702 injection. That feature, added to Ethereum in a 2025 upgrade, lets ordinary wallets temporarily act like smart contracts. Prosecutors said the hackers used it to take control of Binance’s hot wallets and route funds to a “sweeper” contract that moved them out as soon as they arrived. Investigators also traced AVAX that was split up, bridged and swapped until it became about $1.56 million in USDC. U.S. agencies attribute the theft to North Korean military hackers known as the Lazarus Group, or APT38. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Relai Launches Stacks, Letting Bitcoin Savers Split Plans by Goal Swiss bitcoin app Relai launched Stacks on Tuesday, a feature that lets users run several recurring bitcoin savings plans side by side, one for each goal, such as a house, a wedding or a child’s first car. Stacks is live for all Relai users in Switzerland and the European Union. Each Stack carries its own amount and schedule, and users can change either at any time without starting over, the company said. A savings plan is Relai’s version of dollar-cost averaging: buying a fixed amount of bitcoin on a set schedule, weekly or monthly, regardless of price. Savers use it to avoid timing the market. Since September, Relai users have been able to change the amount and buy date of an active plan. Stacks applies that to several goals at once, so a saver can put more toward a house one month, slow down a car fund the next and leave an emergency reserve untouched. In practice, Stacks is an organizing layer, not a new account. Relai’s help pages describe each Stack as a separate pot with its own bitcoin address inside the same wallet. Users get up to five custom Stacks plus a main balance, and moving bitcoin between them takes a regular on-chain transaction with a network fee. Self-custody cuts both ways Relai is self-custodial, meaning it does not hold customers’ bitcoin. The coins in every Stack sit in a wallet controlled by a 12-word recovery phrase, or seed phrase, that only the user has. All Stacks share that one phrase, and restoring the wallet with it brings every Stack back. The trade-off is responsibility. A saver who loses the phrase and the phone has no password reset and no support desk that can recover the coins. Anyone who gets the phrase can take them, which is why attackers have gone as far as tampering with hardware wallets to capture it. “Everyone saves for something. Bitcoin faded to near $61,100 on Monday afternoon after spiking as high as $64,500 on Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO. The slide continued overnight. Bitcoin fell below $60,000 and touched about $59,400 before edging back to the $60,000 line ahead of the U.S. open. entertainment.title: Beyond the Mini LED Label: What Should Define Good Mini LED Performance?
entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. sports.title: Man Utd's Yoro has Anfield red card overturned
sports.description: Leny Yoro was sent off for this tackle on Alexander Isak [Getty Images] Manchester United defender Leny Yoro has had the red card he was shown during Sunday's Premier League match at Liverpool overturned. The Football Association has confirmed Yoro will now be clear to face Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday. "Leny Yoro's one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal," said the FA in a statement. New United head coach Mauricio Pochettino was furious at the decision, which came just eight minutes in and, he felt, changed the course of the game, which Liverpool won 4-0. Liverpool striker Alexander Isak ran on to a ball that bounced over Matthijs de Ligt but took a heavy touch that meant the ball was likely to run through to United goalkeeper Senne Lammens even if Yoro had not brought the Swede down. Nevertheless, referee Sam Barrott sent Yoro off, drawing criticism from Pochettino. "The ball wasn't in his control," he said. "Isak, when he saw the control wasn't good, it's normal to delay, and stop to the run. In that moment that Yoro came from the back, and you go down. "But all that we play football; you know that wasn't intentional. That is never a foul." 'No-one's coming to save us' - but how can Man Utd save themselves? Sporting boss Fonseca dismisses Man Utd fragile talk United have travelled to Lisbon for their next Champions League match on Wednesday (20:00 GMT). The early dismissal of Yoro at Anfield meant Sporting had no chance to assess any changes Pochettino might have made after he replaced Michael Carrick during the international break. But despite United sitting 19th in the Premier League, Sporting boss refuses to accept United are "fragile". "I don't following the reasoning," said Fonseca, who was only appointed on 4 November after the Portuguese club bought him out of his contract at Lyon. "Manchester is a great team," he said. "I don't believe a lot that great teams are fragile. The last game they played in the Champions League, they were trailing 2-0, then won 3-2 against a very difficult opponent in Roma. "Moreover, when they have a new head coach, with such world-class players, it's extremely unpredictable to see if they will have a good day or bad day." United have not won in the Premier League since August and have conceded 19 goals in their past six games in all competitions. Yet, such was the nature of the Liverpool game, Fonseca has had to watch analysis of Pochettino's time in charge of the United States to get an idea of what to expect. "Eight minutes, red card. It's impossible to make an analysis," he said. "I tried to see Pochettino with the United States and what kind of solutions he used. There is some information but it is very difficult to predict." sports.title: Senegal reinstated as Afcon 2025 winners by court ruling
sports.description: Sadio Mane's Senegal have been confirmed as Afcon 2025 winners following their appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, giving the Teranga Lions a second continental title [Getty Images] Senegal have been reinstated as winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations after a ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport. The court's award overturns a previous decision which had stripped the West Africans of the title they won on the pitch during a chaotic final against host nation Morocco in January. The result of that match in Rabat, which saw the Teranga Lions triumph 1-0 after extra time, was overturned almost two months later when a Confederation of African Football (Caf) appeals board decreed Senegal had breached competition regulations by leaving the field of play in second-half stoppage time in protest at a penalty awarded against them. Senegal's football federation (FSF) subsequently appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas), sport's highest legal authority, with a three-man panel hearing its case behind closed doors in Lausanne on 8 October. In a unanimous verdict, the Cas panel has effectively backed the decision by referee Jean-Jacques Ndala to restart the game after Senegal returned to the field and the match was played to a conclusion. The result of the final stands and Senegal are now confirmed as Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) 2025 winners. A statement issued by Cas said the court considered that "the referee's decision to resume the match or to stop it fell definitively within his sole authority". "By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met - both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume." The FSF immediately reacted with a social media post featuring a picture of the side lifting the trophy in January captioned with the phrase "again and always champions of Africa". "The FSF welcomes this ruling with deep satisfaction," it later said in a statement. "This decision affirms, above all, the triumph of sporting fairness and reaffirms a fundamental principle: the true outcome of a match is determined exclusively on the field of play, under the protection of sports law." Meanwhile, Morocco's football federation (FRMF) expressed "surprise" at the ruling and added that it would "pursue all available legal avenues to challenge the decision". Caf is yet to comment but its president Patrice Motsepe has repeatedly said that his organisation will respect and adhere to the Cas ruling. The full grounds for the decision will be published by Cas in due course unless the parties request confidentiality. sports.title: Hackensack-Teaneck Thanksgiving football game rescheduled due to storm
sports.description: Another piece of North Jersey’s fading Thanksgiving football tradition is being pushed off the holiday this year, this time by the weather. The annual rivalry game between Hackensack and Teaneck, a Thanksgiving fixture dating to 1931, has been moved to Wednesday evening as a coastal storm threatens the region with heavy rain and strong winds. Kickoff is now scheduled for 6 p.m. at Teaneck High School. The change leaves one of North Jersey’s longest-running holiday rivalries without its traditional Thanksgiving morning setting. The other remaining Thanksgiving Day game, between Tenafly and Dumont, was also moved to Wednesday night because of the forecast. Story continues below photo gallery. The game was originally scheduled for Thanksgiving morning at 10:30 a.m. Kick-off will now be 6 p.m. Wednesday, Nov. 25, at Teaneck High School. “This decision was made with the safety and well-being of our student-athletes, twirlers, marching band, cheerleading teams, families, and community members as our top priority,” the Teaneck School District wrote in a statement. “We appreciate the understanding and flexibility of our students, families, alumni, and community members as we make this adjustment.” Ed Klimek, Teaneck's athletic director, said the main reason behind the decision was to allow the band, flag twirlers and cheerleaders, who had been practicing for weeks, to be able to perform. "Two years ago we played in an absolute monsoon," he said. "We can play football in the rain, but they can't perform in the rain. When I proposed this to Hackensack and to the football teams, everyone was on board." The parade to the field before the game, with the two teams’ school bands, cheerleaders and flag twirlers marching, is canceled, Klimek said. The traditional Thanksgiving Day team between the neighboring communities is one of the last played in North Jersey on the holiday. Many high school football teams have done away with the tradition of playing on Thanksgiving over the years, because of difficulties with the schedule and concerns that it would interfere with teams’ preparations for playing in championship games. The other remaining game scheduled for Thanksgiving Day between Tenafly and Dumont was also rescheduled to 6 p.m. Wednesday and will be played at Geissinger Field in Tenafly. The annual Thanksgiving Day rivalry game between Hackensack Comets and Teaneck Highwaymen dates back to 1931. Teaneck’s record for the season is 7-3. Hackensack is 4-4. Hackensack has dominated the matchup in recent years and has won the past 12 meetings between the two. sports.description: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen certainly could have been called for unsportsmanlike conduct in a recent defeat of the Miami Dolphins , but wasn't. Johnson was blocking Allen near a sideline when Allen appeared to fling him to ground by a facemask. Allen then shoved Johnson again when they are out of bounds. Was it a simple football play? Or should it have been a 15-yard penalty? Johnson said: "I saw J-Rod get the pick and from there on, I'm looking for a block. It just happened to be Josh Allen. I guess he didn't appreciate it much. Nearly a year after that chaotic final in Morocco, Senegal can again celebrate its victory. The CAS ruling is not simply a triumph for the Senegal’s national team. It is also an important affirmation of the principles that should govern the sport: The authority of the match referee, the integrity of the result and the distinction between disciplinary regulations and decisions made during a game. The final was undoubtedly controversial. Senegal defeated Morocco 1-0 after extra time, but the game was overshadowed by a dramatic incident in second-half stoppage time. With the game still scoreless, Morocco was awarded a penalty kick. Senegal’s players protested the decision by leaving the field, resulting in a 15-minute delay. Congolese referee Jean-Jacques Ndala eventually allowed the game to resume. Morocco’s Brahim Diaz subsequently missed the penalty, then Senegal went on to score the decisive goal in extra time and win the game. There was little doubt that Senegal’s walk-off was an unacceptable response to a referee’s decision. Players cannot abandon a match because they disagree with a call. The tournament’s own regulations also provided for a team that refuses to play or leaves the field without the referee’s permission to forfeit the contest. The central question was never whether Senegal’s conduct deserved scrutiny. It was whether the circumstances justified overturning a completed match and later awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory by default. The Confederation of African Football’s appeals panel thought so when it ruled in March that Senegal had forfeited the Jan. 18 final. CAS has now correctly rejected that interpretation. The distinction is crucial. Tournament regulations exist to establish order, protect competition integrity and provide sanctions when teams refuse to fulfill their obligations. sports.title: Bundesliga planning new Saturday night kick-off time from 2029/30
sports.description: Bundesliga planning new Saturday night kick-off time from 2029/30 The Bundesliga could introduce a new Saturday evening kick-off time from the 2029/30 season as part of the next domestic television rights cycle. According to Bild, plans are being drawn up to stage five marquee Bundesliga fixtures per season at 20:30 CET on Saturday evenings. The proposal was reportedly well received at a meeting of the 36 Bundesliga and 2. Bundesliga clubs in Frankfurt at the beginning of October, with the prospect of attracting larger television audiences in a prime-time slot appealing to potential broadcasters. Crucially, the traditional Saturday 15:30 kick-off time would remain unaffected, as would the existing 18:30 slot. Instead, four fixtures that would ordinarily take place at 19:30 on Sunday evenings would be moved to the new Saturday night slot. The fifth fixture would come from the Friday evening slot on the Easter weekend, with Bundesliga matches not taking place on Good Friday. The proposed changes would coincide with the start of the next domestic broadcasting rights cycle in the summer of 2029.

sports.title: Retina Dynamics Brings Robotics to the Breaking Boom
sports.description: “There are only so many ways breakers can really differentiate themselves in the market. Operational efficiency is one.” Joseph Owens, former Senior Manager of Live Commerce at Fanatics Live, told me that reality was the driving principle behind his new hardware company, Retina Dynamics. Owens founded the company alongside Matthew Harfmann and Sheridan Skala, with founding engineers Jack Scalise and Eli Thummel leading the technical build. During his tenure at Fanatics, Owens identified back-end logistics as one of the single biggest pain point for breakers, noting that almost every major operator struggled with the tedious, time-consuming process of manually sorting cards after massive product releases . To help alleviate the operations backlog, Retina Dynamics is introducing what it claims is the first automated, robotic sorter built explicitly for breakers and sports card consignment sellers . By introducing a robotic sorting machine to the industry, Owens aims to solve that bottleneck without eliminating jobs . The technology is not designed to replace the human workforce; rather, it allows owners to reallocate those employees away from mundane sorting tasks and into roles that drive better business value, such as customer service, expedited shipping, and social marketing . View this post on Instagram A post shared by Joe (@adhdcollector_joe) The Hardware and Safety Measures The solution is a machine roughly the size of a pinball cabinet . The Retina Dynamics robot uses custom-built, in-house scanning software paired with a specialized “claw” to identify, sort, and organize trading cards . Crucially, the machine is designed to safely handle cards whether they are raw, penny-sleeved, or secured in rigid top-loaders . As a secondary benefit, it captures high-resolution, front-and-back scans of every card as it passes through the system, which can be seamlessly exported for consignment listings . According to Owens, extensive testing went into the physics of the claw to ensure the sorting speed matches human efficiency without risking edge or surface damage to the cards . Pricing and Market Availability The systems are currently being assembled in-house by the company’s full-time engineering team . Production is capped at roughly 15 to 20 units per month to ensure quality control and maintain a manageable 120-day lead time for new buyers . Early demand has already outpaced initial supply: Retina Dynamics has sold out of its initial 20-unit run for November and will reopen for additional pre-orders on December 5. The base unit is priced at $25,000, with an additional $450 monthly subscription required to cover the API data costs associated with reading and identifying the cards . For larger operations requiring three or more machines, the hardware price drops to $22,500 per unit . For more information and to view the sorting machines in action, collectors and breakers can visit retinadynamics.ai .

sports.title: Denny Hamlin Sets Hard Line On NASCAR Retirement Plans
sports.description: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Denny Hamlin has made his stance clear to the NASCAR world . The 46-year-old driver plans to end his full-time Cup Series career after the 2027 season. He will not stick around just to fill a seat if his skills fade. This decision comes despite strong pressure from team owner Joe Gibbs to reconsider the timeline. Hamlin told SiriusXM NASCAR Radio that his final call depends entirely on his ability to win races every weekend. Joe Gibbs has been trying to change Hamlin’s mind for some time. The team owner visits the driver’s home in the evenings to discuss the future. Hamlin described these late-night talks on the couch as a normal part of their relationship. “Joe does his normal thing. He just pops in at the house at 8-9 p.m. at night and sits on the couch and has a discussion with you. That’s already started,” Hamlin said, according to MotorBiscuit . The conversations have begun, but the driver’s mind seems set on a specific path. Winning Is the Only Option Hamlin refuses to drive a car he cannot win with. He knows that staying in the sport without a chance at victory would feel wrong. The driver explained that his competitive fire is what keeps him behind the wheel. “If I know that I’m not going to be able to win every single weekend, there’s just no way I can do it,” Hamlin said. This standard is non-negotiable for a driver with his track record. He finished third in the Cup Series standings last year and won four races. The driver also wants to protect the legacy of Joe Gibbs Racing. He plans to ensure the team has a new driver ready before he steps away. Hamlin does not want to leave the organization in a bind or hold back their progress. “I want to make sure they’ve got their next driver planned, lined up — all that stuff. I’m definitely going to do whatever is best for Joe Gibbs Racing, but I’m not going to compromise my performance,” Hamlin said. He values the team but will not sacrifice his own speed to help them. The Clock Is Ticking Hamlin admits that his body feels the toll of racing more than it used to. He senses that his physical edge is slipping away slowly. This feeling in daily life is a warning sign for his time on the track. “I can feel it. In my everyday life, I can tell things are changing. It’s a matter of time before it changes on the racetrack. It just is. I want to avoid that at all costs,” Hamlin said. He wants to leave while he is still at the top of his game. Hamlin is not making this choice based on money or contract terms. He noted that Gibbs has been fair with him throughout his 21-year career. The decision is purely about pride and the desire to compete at the highest level. He feels content with the idea of hanging up his helmet after two more years. Hamlin also said he wants to talk to retired drivers like Kevin Harvick to learn from their experiences.

sports.description: Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur. Getty (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Getty The Green Bay Packers offensive line has had anything but continuity through the 2026 season. While head coach Matt LaFleur admitted that this has been a major issue for the team, he also acknowledged that there is a chance for them to find continuity between their bye week and the end of the season. “I think continuity is critical,” said LaFleur when discussing offensive line continuity. “Especially when you’re talking about the offensive line, where you need five guys working as one. So I think that is a huge component in terms of your ability to go out there and have consistent success.” The Packers coach added that experience is also important. “I also think just, you know, the experience of that group up front plays a pivotal role in that as well,” added LaFleur. The Packers have only had Jordan Morgan at left tackle start every game at the same position. They have had multiple starters at the four other spots. Green Bay Packers Hoping to Find Offensive Line Continuity Getty (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Now, the team has a chance to find some continuity. Jordan Morgan is still at left tackle and Anthony Belton has been starting at right tackle since Week 3. They are high on Laken Tomlinson at left guard, and if Kevin Zeitler and Sean Rhyan are healthy, they are going to start at right guard and center, respectively. As long as there are not any injuries this unit is going to be what leads the team into a playoff push. While LaFleur is excited to see the continuity, his message to the unit is to handle what they have to. “You know, my thing is this: it really— at the end of the day, it doesn’t matter,” said LaFleur. “You got a job to go, and you got to go perform well. And if you don’t, then it’s going to get scrutinized, and it is what it is. But it’s never an excuse. You still— that’s why you prepare everybody.” Packers Not Making Excuses LaFleur noted that he thinks that everyone on the roster needs to be ready to be called into duty. “I mean, whether you’re on the active or you’re a P-squad guy, you got to be ready to play, and you got to be ready to do your part. So it’s just— it’s the circumstance that every team in the league faces.” It almost comes off as if LaFleur realized in his first answer that he was making an excuse of not having continuity and then tried to defend it by saying that the depth has to be ready. Still, depth or not, those players would be best with continuity and experience as well We will see how many games Green Bay can roll with their projected five. They play the Los Angeles Rams in Week 12. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Why Packers’ Offensive Line Could Look Different After Bye appeared first on HEAVY .

technology.title: Homo erectus lived in the rainforest alongside Denisovans
technology.description: Homo erectus was walking around mainland Asia at least 60,000 years more recently than archaeologists thought. A handful of teeth from two caves in southern China's Guangxi Province just filled in a significant gap in the fossil record of a region that's vital to the story of how our genus, Homo , took over the world. The chemical makeup of the teeth's enamel suggests that, over the course of their lives, these Homo erectus moved across surprisingly large distances and made their living in dense tropical rainforests—an environment we'd previously assumed that only our species had ever gained a real foothold in. And one of the teeth offers a strong clue that Homo erectus probably shared this vast landscape with the Denisovans. A handful of teeth with a lot to say Baxian and Naxian are a pair of limestone caves that lie 15 kilometers apart along a karst valley corridor in southern China. University of Copenhagen paleoanthropologist Frido Welker and his colleagues unearthed a total of nine hominin teeth from among the more than 18,000 bones and fragments from non-hominin animals found there. Macquarie University paleoanthropologist Kira Westaway and her colleagues analyzed proteins and chemical isotopes from the enamel of five of these teeth. Read full article Comments

technology.title: Microsoft brings serverless PostgreSQL into Fabric to bridge transactions and analytics
technology.description: Microsoft has brought its HorizonDB PostgreSQL service into public preview in Fabric, aiming to bring transactional and analytical workloads closer together. The corporation says applications can submit queries through a single PostgreSQL endpoint, with transactional and analytical work handled by the appropriate engines. Analysts said the move follows similar efforts by Databricks and Snowflake to combine operational databases with analytics. But tighter integration with Microsoft's stack could make applications harder to move elsewhere. Fabric HorizonDB joins SQL database and Cosmos DB in Microsoft's Fabric database portfolio. "By bringing operational databases, analytics, and AI together on a unified, governed platform, developers can build intelligent applications with less data movement and complexity. Fabric HorizonDB will also serve as the PostgreSQL backend for Fabric apps," Microsoft said. Microsoft first unveiled Azure HorizonDB in preview in November 2025 and made it generally available last week. It competes with other cloud database services and distributed systems such as CockroachDB and YugabyteDB, both of which support PostgreSQL's wire protocol. At the time, it said HorizonDB would offer "massive read scale without the need to replicate the database between instances." Speaking to The Register last week, Shireesh Thota, veep of Azure databases and Fabric applications, said that bringing the system into Fabric – its platform for data lakes, data warehouses, and analytics launched in 2023 – would connect operational data in HorizonDB with analytical data in OneLake, Fabric's unified data lake. "Once the data hits the OneLake storage, you can have analytical engines that take advantage of it. In HorizonDB, the PostgreSQL query engine can talk to the distributed query engine that we use in our Fabric data warehouse. We're fusing these query engines, thereby enabling the developers to submit a query that has pieces of the query that can work on OLTP and pieces of the query that can work on OLAP," he said. "The application need not worry about two endpoints, or about consistency of data and all that complexity. They can just talk to HorizonDB as a Fabric endpoint, and they can submit all these queries. We are basically operationalizing in OneLake." Operational data remains in HorizonDB's database storage, while mirroring maintains an analytical copy in OneLake, introduced in 2023 , which replicates a snapshot of the external database to OneLake in Delta Parquet tables and keeps the replica synced in "near real time." Thota said the process would not affect the transactional system. "Our core goal is to never impact OLTP workload while we are doing this, and we succeed [by] reading off the log as an additional replica to do this mirroring," he said. technology.description: Jensen Huang was barely back in charge of Nvidia when Uncle Sam slapped Megaspeed –­ the Singaporean cloud provider at the center of the scandal that cost him his job ­­– on its trade blacklist. The US Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has added Megaspeed and a number of affiliated businesses to its Entity List, restricting their access to American technology amid an ongoing investigation into the suspected diversion of advanced GPUs to China. The final rule [PDF], filed Monday afternoon and scheduled for publication in the Federal Register on Wednesday, names seven businesses across Singapore, Malaysia, and Thailand, including Megaspeed's owner, Swiftdata, and Malaysian subsidiary Speedmatrix. Also in Washington's crosshairs is Apex Enterprise Solutions, a Singapore-based subsidiary of Chinese cloud computing giant Alibaba. BIS said the businesses posed a significant risk of diverting advanced computing hardware to recipients or applications not authorized by the US government. Anyone looking to supply the seven companies with goods subject to US export controls will need a license, with applications subject to a "presumption of denial." Despite the timing of Monday's announcement, the US government's interest in Megaspeed predates the revelations about Jensen Huang's private life by some considerable margin. In a joint statement issued last week, the Departments of Justice and Commerce confirmed that the latter had opened an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 after spotting suspicious activity while monitoring potential violations of semiconductor export controls. Investigators requested records from Nvidia relating to both direct and indirect sales to Megaspeed in May 2025, and the GPU giant put the Singaporean outfit on its internal "no sell" list the following month. US investigators, accompanied by Singaporean law enforcement officials, subsequently visited Megaspeed's premises and interviewed its then-CEO, Alice Huang. The Justice Department has since taken the lead on the criminal investigation. Alice Huang, who is not related to the Nvidia boss, is a businesswoman with whom Jensen was said to be having an affair – he admitted to extramarital infidelity earlier this month , although he never name-checked the Megaspeed exec. According to reports, US intelligence officials suspected she was working on behalf of Chinese intelligence, though Beijing has rejected the espionage allegations. Megaspeed maintains that its business is lawful and says Alice Huang formally left the company in August last year. It has also enlisted outside lawyers to conduct an internal investigation. Nvidia's own Huang lasted all of 11 days in corporate exile.
